sources.title: Nini Havela Dishong, Bukit Choras Archaeological Complex: Geophysical and Geo-Archaeological Analysis (USM, 2022)
sources.note: Direct university thesis abstract: Kedah as several riverine and coastal settlements, second to fourteenth centuries; laterite structures, water tanks, inscription, nails and geophysical methods. Abstract does not date the tanks precisely or establish toilets.

sources.title: Daniel Perret and Heddy Surachman, Jejak-Jejak Persia di Barus, AMERTA 25.1 (2007), pages 1 to 11
sources.note: Original full PDF directly read at article/download/3169/2172. Issue is 2007 despite later platform upload. Pages 2 to 4: Lobu Tua dating, fortification, camphor, pottery, stone containers and possible eyebrow pencil; Bukit Hasang continuity. Distinct article from the already budget-limited Mapping the Acehnese Past chapter.

sources.title: Museum Nasional Indonesia, Prasasti Lobu Tua, collection D.42
sources.note: Full indexed original museum description: Tamil language and script, 1088, Barus merchant guild and taxes. Direct page presents a challenge. Its explanation of deliberate later breaking is a legend and is not adopted.

sources.title: Ludvik Kalus, La plus ancienne inscription islamique du Monde malais?, Archipel 59 (2000), pages 23 to 24
sources.note: Page 23 directly read; page 24 complete original indexed under ?pageId=T1_24. Find from 1997 outside stratigraphy. Scholar tentatively dates seal to tenth or eleventh century and reads second line Muhammad. First line reading and talisman function uncertain. Modern Arabic transcription is normalized from his reading, not an independent visual decipherment.

sources.title: Zuliskandar Ramli, Nik Hassan Shuhaimi Nik Abdul Rahman and Abdul Latif Samian, X-ray fluorescent analysis on Indo-Pacific glass beads from Sungai Mas archaeological sites (2011)
sources.note: Direct publisher abstract, Journal of Radioanalytical and Nuclear Chemistry 287, pages 741 to 747: 22 samples, nine major and nine trace elements, colorants and opacity, conclusion of local manufacture in sixth to thirteenth centuries. Only abstract-supported results used.

sources.title: USM Global Archaeology Research Centre, Largest Buddhist temple structure unearthed in Bukit Choras (2023)
sources.note: Direct research-centre republication of New Straits Times report of project announcement. Eighth to ninth century, life-sized stucco statues, exposed walls and stairs, comparisons with Sumatra and West Java. Comparative style does not establish political annexation.

sources.title: USM, Jumpaan arca berbentuk manusia yang lengkap di Tapak Warisan Arkeologi Bukit Choras (26 June 2024)
sources.note: Direct primary project report: April to May 2024 field phase; stucco consists of lime, water and sand; Buddha beside north wall; temporary removal to USM conservation laboratory. Separate announcement from 2023 report.

sources.title: Yohan Chabot and colleagues, Geoarcheological Study of the Kota Cina Site, Archipel Hors-Série 4 (2024)
sources.note: Original article/PDF indexed sections 44 to 53 and conclusion, pages 7 and 18; direct publisher blocked. Wood and palm-fibre cords, broad eleventh to thirteenth century dates, shell middens, siltation and tentative early fourteenth-century abandonment explanation. Whole Kota Cina 2024 volume treated as one budgeted work. Site outside these decoded polygons, explicitly a regional comparison.

proposedOverrides.name: Minor Hindu and Buddhist states
proposedOverrides.summary: Changing ports and religious communities of Sumatra, the Malay Peninsula and parts of Borneo.

batchIdentityNotes: Exact missing record 800 to 1279; no association with the Borneo/Sulawesi kingdoms label of 1300 to 1492 or the mixed India/islands minor Hindu kingdoms label of 1279 to 1400. Named Srivijaya, Brunei and later Islamic states remain separate. Detailed local point checks are in the parent folder. No claim that trade goods prove ethnic identity, centralized control, universal faith or specific family arrangements. No securely sourced local school, hospital or toilet description was found; material learning, grooming and water evidence are used within their limits. Kota Cina is explicitly outside the polygon. Barus lies outside after 900; Kedah outside at 1200.
